bullets.title: Leading Medication Safety and Clinical Governance
bullets.text: Medication safety is an organisational responsibility supported by governance, leadership, policy, education and monitoring. Nurse leaders influence whether staff feel able to question unsafe orders, report incidents and learn from mistakes.

bullets.title: Human Factors and Systems Thinking in Medication Error Prevention
bullets.text: Many medication errors occur within complex systems involving people, packaging, technology, workflow and communication. Systems thinking looks beyond the final action and identifies the conditions that made error possible.

bullets.title: Quality Improvement, Pharmacovigilance and Medication Stewardship
bullets.text: Global Nursing Professionals use data to understand medication harm and test improvements. They also contribute to pharmacovigilance by identifying adverse reactions and to stewardship by promoting appropriate, evidence-informed use of medicines.

bullets.title: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
bullets.text: Electronic prescribing, barcode administration, smart pumps and clinical decision support can improve medication safety. They can also introduce new risks such as alert fatigue, incorrect data and over-reliance on automation. Global professionals use technology critically and share learning across systems.
